questions.q: The king, queen and jack of clubs are removed from a standard 52-card deck. One card is drawn from the remaining deck. What are P(heart) and P(king), respectively?
questions.explanation: After removing three club face cards, 49 cards remain. No heart was removed, so all 13 hearts are still present, giving P(heart)=13/49. One king, the king of clubs, was removed, leaving 3 kings, so P(king)=3/49.

questions.q: Two ordinary dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the product of the two top numbers is less than 9?
questions.explanation: There are 36 equally likely ordered outcomes. Counting products below 9 gives 6 outcomes when the first die is 1, then 4, 2, 2, 1 and 1 outcomes for first-die values 2 through 6, for a total of 16. Thus the probability is 16/36 = 4/9.

questions.q: Two ordinary dice are thrown. What is the probability that the absolute difference between the two numbers is 2?
questions.explanation: The favourable ordered pairs are (1,3), (2,4), (3,1), (3,5), (4,2), (4,6), (5,3) and (6,4). That gives 8 favourable outcomes out of 36 equally likely outcomes. Therefore the probability is 8/36 = 2/9.

questions.q: Each of two dice has faces marked 0,1,1,1,6,6. If both are thrown, what is the probability that the total score is 7?
questions.explanation: A total of 7 occurs only as 1+6 or 6+1. On each die, P(1)=3/6 and P(6)=2/6. Therefore P(total 7) = 2 x (3/6)(2/6) = 12/36 = 1/3.
